summary:
Mission Control: Mars Outpost is an interactive Mars colony survival simulation developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge.

Players take command of ARES-01, a fictional four-person research outpost at Jezero Crater, and must keep their crew alive for 30 Martian sols. They manage essential life-support resources, assign astronaut duties, maintain habitat systems, respond to unpredictable environmental emergencies, and complete scientific exploration objectives.

The simulation features dynamic weather, decision-based events, resource management, crew specializations, mission telemetry, and an AI-assisted mission advisor. Every decision affects the mission's survival and scientific progress.

Our goal is to make the engineering challenges of human exploration on Mars accessible and engaging through an interactive experience that encourages strategic thinking, resource management, and curiosity about planetary science.
details:
Overview

Mission Control: Mars Outpost is a browser-based interactive simulation designed to introduce users to the challenges of establishing and maintaining a human research outpost on Mars.

The player assumes the role of commander of ARES-01, a fictional four-person research mission located at Jezero Crater. The objective is to survive 30 Martian sols while maintaining essential life-support systems, protecting the crew, and completing scientific exploration objectives.

How It Works

The simulation revolves around interconnected resource-management and decision-making mechanics.

1. Life Support Management

Players manage six essential resources: energy, water, oxygen, food, radiation protection, and crew health. Habitat integrity and supporting subsystem conditions are tracked separately.

2. Crew Management

Four astronauts have different specializations, including mission command, medicine, engineering, and geology. Players assign activities to crew members, and their specializations influence mission outcomes.

3. Dynamic Environmental Events

The simulation features 13 events, including dust storms, solar particle events, oxygen leaks, equipment failures, and unexpected scientific discoveries. Players must evaluate available options and manage their consequences.

4. Scientific Exploration

Players collect geological samples and conduct scientific experiments. Completing research objectives contributes to the final mission evaluation.

5. Mission Intelligence

A mission advisor analyses the current simulation state and provides recommendations based on resource levels, crew health, environmental threats, and mission progress. A rule-based advisor works without requiring an external API.

6. Mission Telemetry

Interactive charts track resource trends and mission conditions, helping players understand how their decisions influence the outpost over time.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project transforms abstract space-exploration challenges into an interactive learning experience. Instead of simply reading about the difficulties of living on Mars, users experience the trade-offs involved in maintaining life-support systems, managing limited resources, responding to emergencies, and prioritizing scientific objectives.

It encourages strategic thinking, problem-solving, resource allocation, and interest in planetary science and human space exploration.

Technology Used

  • React and TypeScript
  • Vite
  • Tailwind CSS
  • Framer Motion
  • Recharts
  • Lucide React
  • LocalStorage
  • Procedural Web Audio

The application uses a modular simulation engine with game logic separated from the user interface.

Creativity and Innovation

The project combines educational content with strategy-game mechanics. Environmental events, astronaut specializations, resource dependencies, and evolving mission conditions ensure that decisions have consequences.

The interface is designed as a futuristic mission-control system to make the player feel responsible for operating a Mars research outpost.

The simulation is intentionally simplified for educational gameplay and is not intended to represent a real engineering or life-support model.

Scientific Foundation

Environmental concepts and Martian facts are informed by publicly available NASA resources. The game references Martian weather, atmospheric conditions, temperature, radiation challenges, and communication delays.

ARES-01, its astronauts, and its mission scenarios are fictional.
